brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — ESource WhiteLabel Sales Course

questions.question: What are the three main reasons firms buy our white-label bookkeeping tool?
choices: Their brand, data stays home, and lower cost per client
Bank feeds, unlimited staff, and mobile app access
Payroll integration, client login portal, and Excel exports
QuickBooks compatibility, Xero integration, and Wave support
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—these three reasons are the core value proposition you should be able to say in one breath.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The three reasons are their brand on client reports, data security (stays home), and lower cost per client. The other options mix in competitor features or features we don't yet offer.

questions.question: What is the ideal firm size and type to target with this tool?
choices: Solo CPAs with 1 to 5 clients who want mobile access
Large accounting firms with 200+ clients using QuickBooks Online
Bookkeeping and small CPA firms with roughly 5 to 100 monthly clients
Tax preparation firms that only do annual filings
questions.feedback_correct: That's the sweet spot—firms in that range have the scale to benefit and the independence to make their own software choice.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Our best fit is bookkeeping and small CPA firms with 5 to 100 monthly clients who want their own brand and care about client privacy. Solo practitioners or mega-firms don't match our positioning.

questions.question: According to the course, what should you do before running a demo?
choices: Send the prospect a pricing sheet and ask them to review it
Ask discovery questions about their current tools, costs, brand visibility, and time spent on transactions
Show them the firm-branded screen with their logo immediately to create excitement
Schedule a follow-up meeting to discuss implementation details
questions.feedback_correct: Discovery questions uncover pain and help you tailor the demo to what actually matters to them—you'll repeat their own words back to them during the demo and close.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While the logo is impactful, discovery questions come first so you understand their situation and can speak directly to their pain points instead of giving a generic demo.

questions.question: What is the proposed pricing structure for our tool?
choices: Flat rate of $20 per month per firm, unlimited clients
$20 for the first client, $17 for clients 2–10, $15 for 11–30, and $14 for 31–100
Tiered by staff seats: $10 per seat up to 5 seats, then $5 per additional seat
$26.60 per client per month, matching QuickBooks Online pricing
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the tiers are graduated per client, and staff seats are unlimited, which is a key advantage over competitors.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The proposed structure charges per active client book in graduated bands: $20, $17, $15, and $14 as the firm grows, and staff seats don't cost extra. Always remember to say 'proposed' until pricing is final.

questions.question: How should you address a prospect's concern that their clients are already familiar with QuickBooks?
choices: Agree it's a problem and suggest they switch to QuickBooks Online instead
Explain that clients get Excel reports with the firm's name on them and don't need to learn any software
Tell them QuickBooks is outdated and our tool is more modern
Offer a discount on the first three months to make the transition easier
questions.feedback_correct: That's the right angle—clients never see or interact with the tool; they only see professional Excel reports with the firm's brand, so familiarity with QBO is irrelevant.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Clients don't use the software directly; they receive Excel reports branded with the accounting firm's name. Familiarity with QuickBooks is not a real objection once you explain this.

questions.question: What does 'data stays home' mean as a value proposition?
choices: Firms can only access the tool from their office building
Client bank statements never leave the firm's computers, and books and backups are locked so only signed-in staff can open them
The tool only works offline and requires manual syncing
Client data is stored in the firm's QuickBooks account, not in the cloud
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—this is a powerful differentiator because no competitor can claim data never leaves the firm's computers, and backups stay locked to the firm.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Data stays home means the firm maintains full control: bank statements and backups stay on their computers and are locked, so only their authorized staff can access the books.

questions.question: If a prospect says they need bank feeds before they'll switch, how should you respond?
choices: Tell them we're building feeds and will have them in three months
Acknowledge they're important and offer to connect them with our product team
Explain that monthly downloads take minutes and every month is proven to tie to the bank, which many firms prefer to feeds that silently miss transactions
Admit it's a gap and suggest they stay with their current system
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—you're not dismissing the concern; you're reframing it honestly and showing how our approach actually solves the problem better in many cases.
questions.feedback_incorrect: This objection is common, and the response is to explain how monthly downloads actually work well in practice and offer a transparency advantage that live feeds don't have.

questions.question: What is the demo sequence you should follow, and why does the logo placement matter?
choices: Show the P&L first to prove financial accuracy, then upload the bank statement, then show the logo—this builds trust gradually
Open the firm-branded screen with their logo first (ideally pre-loaded), then upload a bank statement, show Ask Client, and finish with Health dashboard and reports—the logo is the moment that sells
Start with the pricing page so they understand the cost, then show the demo to confirm it fits their budget
Show all the advanced features first to demonstrate capability, then reveal the branding at the end as a bonus
questions.feedback_correct: Yes—the branded screen with their logo is the emotional high point of the demo and seals the "this is for me" feeling before you show the mechanics.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The logo moment comes early in the demo (first thing after opening), not at the end. This is when they see their own brand on the screen, which is powerful and shouldn't be buried.

questions.question: How should you close a sale with a prospect who is hesitant about switching all their clients at once?
choices: Push for a full commitment and offer a steep discount to overcome their objection
Propose a pilot of 3 to 5 clients for 60 days alongside their current system, agree on success measures, and then scale after the pilot succeeds
Suggest they take two weeks to decide while keeping the deal open
Start with one client free for 30 days as a trial to prove the value
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—a small pilot removes risk and lets success speak for itself, which is how most deals close in this playbook.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The closing strategy is always a pilot: small scale (3–5 clients), limited time (60 days), alongside their current system for safety, with agreed success measures. This is how you overcome hesitation and move to a full rollout.

questions.question: You're in a sales call and the prospect asks about data security after an employee leaves the firm. What story should you tell them?
choices: Explain that our cloud servers are protected by military-grade encryption and ESource never has access to client data
Tell them that employee access is logged and they can review the audit trail to see what was accessed
Describe how only the owner can add sign-in users, how removing someone locks their computer out at next check-in, and how backups are locked to the firm so an employee can't take data home
Admit that we don't have a perfect solution and suggest they keep their current system for sensitive client data
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—this is the owner's security story and it's your most powerful answer to a real concern: your clients stay yours, and you control exactly who can access them.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The security story focuses on the owner's control: they add users, they remove them, and the system locks former employees out even on their personal devices. Backups are locked too, so employees can't steal data. This is what owners care about most.
